items.q: Fatigable ptosis and diplopia worsening by evening with anti acetylcholine receptor antibodies is treated symptomatically first with what?
items.exp: Pyridostigmine is the oral symptomatic mainstay in myasthenia gravis, prolonging acetylcholine action at the depleted junction. Immunotherapy and thymectomy modify disease but act slowly.
r: Incorrect. Edrophonium is ultrashort and diagnostic historically.
Correct. Pyridostigmine gives sustained symptomatic relief.
Incorrect. Atropine would block needed cholinergic transmission.
Incorrect. Oximes treat organophosphate poisoning, not autoimmunity.
items.kp: Evening fatigable weakness: pyridostigmine for symptoms.

items.q: Which anticholinesterase crosses the blood brain barrier and reverses central anticholinergic delirium?
items.exp: Physostigmine is a tertiary amine entering the brain, reversing delirium from atropine like poisoning. Quaternary agents remain peripheral and cannot help central signs.
r: Incorrect. Neostigmine is quaternary and peripheral.
Incorrect. Pyridostigmine also stays peripheral.
Correct. Physostigmine enters the central nervous system.
Incorrect. Edrophonium is brief and peripheral.
items.kp: Central reversal needs the tertiary amine physostigmine.

items.q: A farmer collapses with miosis, salivation, bronchospasm and fasciculations after spraying. First life saving drug is what?
items.exp: Atropine blocks lethal muscarinic bronchospasm, secretions and bradycardia in organophosphate poisoning and is titrated to dry chest and adequate heart rate. Oxime follows early but never replaces atropine.
r: Incorrect. Oxime alone leaves muscarinic death unblocked.
Correct. Atropine first, titrated generously.
Incorrect. More cholinesterase inhibition worsens poisoning.
Incorrect. Flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines only.
items.kp: Wet, pinpoint and wheezy after spraying: atropine saves life.

items.q: Pralidoxime helps organophosphate poisoning mainly by doing what?
items.exp: Oximes nucleophilically remove the phosphoryl group from inhibited enzyme, restoring activity mainly at nicotinic sites, provided ageing has not made the bond permanent.
r: Incorrect. That is atropine's muscarinic blockade.
Correct. Oximes reactivate enzyme before ageing.
Incorrect. Paralysis is the poison's nicotinic outcome, not therapy.
Incorrect. Oximes act on enzyme, not chelation.
items.kp: Oxime window closes when the enzyme ages.

items.q: A myasthenic on high pyridostigmine doses develops weakness WITH salivation, miosis and fasciculations. This is what?
items.exp: Excess anticholinesterase overstimulates then depolarisation blocks the junction, adding muscarinic flooding signs to weakness. Withholding drug and supportive ventilation distinguish management from myasthenic crisis.
r: Incorrect. More drug deepens cholinergic blockade.
Correct. Flooding signs mark cholinergic excess.
Incorrect. Thymoma does not cause acute muscarinic flooding.
Incorrect. Lambert Eaton improves with activity and lacks these signs.
items.kp: Weak plus wet and twitching means too much drug.

items.q: Neostigmine reversal of neuromuscular blockade is paired with glycopyrrolate mainly to prevent what?
items.exp: Neostigmine raises acetylcholine at muscarinic sites too, slowing heart and flooding glands. Glycopyrrolate shields those sites without entering brain, while nicotinic reversal proceeds.
r: Incorrect. Muscarinic stimulation slows rather than races the heart.
Correct. The partner blocks bradycardia and secretions.
Incorrect. Central effects are minimal with quaternary drugs.
Incorrect. Temperature rise is not the pairing reason.
items.kp: Reverse the junction, shield the heart and glands.

items.q: Donepezil relieves Alzheimer symptoms by which mechanism?
items.exp: Donepezil is a centrally acting reversible cholinesterase inhibitor raising cortical acetylcholine modestly. Memantine is the NMDA blocker partner in moderate disease.
r: Incorrect. Blockade would worsen cognition like anticholinergic delirium.
Correct. Central cholinesterase inhibition is its action.
Incorrect. Dopamine agonism belongs to Parkinson therapy.
Incorrect. NMDA blockade describes memantine.
items.kp: Donepezil raises brain acetylcholine; memantine blocks NMDA.

items.q: Ageing in organophosphate poisoning refers to what?
o: Enzyme inhibitor bond becoming permanent so oximes fail
items.exp: Ageing is dealkylation of the phosphorylated enzyme complex making reactivation impossible, after which recovery awaits new enzyme synthesis over weeks.
r: Incorrect. Ageing is chemical, not demographic.
Correct. The bond matures beyond oxime reversal.
Incorrect. Evaporation does not define ageing.
Incorrect. Atropine remains effective after ageing.
items.kp: Treat early: aged enzyme cannot be reactivated.

items.q: Which feature separates organophosphate from pure muscarinic mushroom poisoning at the bedside?
items.exp: Both flood muscarinic sites, but only cholinesterase poisoning adds nicotinic fasciculations progressing to paralysis and central seizures, needing oxime plus atropine.
r: Incorrect. Salivation occurs in both muscarinic states.
Correct. Fasciculations are the nicotinic fingerprint.
Incorrect. Pinpoint pupils occur in both.
Incorrect. Gut flooding occurs in both.
items.kp: Twitching muscles point to cholinesterase poisoning.

items.q: Thymectomy and immunosuppression in myasthenia gravis are needed because pyridostigmine does what?
o: Relieves symptoms without modifying receptor autoimmunity
items.exp: Cholinesterase inhibition only prolongs transmitter survival; antibody production continues, so steroids, immunotherapy and thymectomy (especially with thymoma or early generalised disease) change the course.
r: Incorrect. Symptomatic drugs never cure autoimmunity.
Correct. Disease modification needs immune therapy.
Incorrect. Drugs do not remove thymoma; surgery does.
Incorrect. It raises, not blocks, junctional transmission.
items.kp: Symptoms eased is not disease modified.
